宏福苑火災引起各界對維修工程圍標問題的關注。競委會今年1月曾搜查14間工程承辦商和顧問公司，涉及在全港17個維修工程從事圍標等行為，估計合約總值約七億港元。行動中取得的證據揭發存在另一個圍標集團，競委會今日再搜查4間承辦商、涉及28個大廈維修工程、總值約五億元，涉嫌在投標期間提交「掩護式」標書等。

The Competition Commission announced yesterday (the 12th) that it had launched a second round of enforcement action in a bid-rigging case involving building maintenance works, searching 12 premises including the offices of four contractors and the residences of individuals involved. The works in question span maintenance projects at 28 estates and buildings, with contracts preliminarily estimated at around HK$500 million in total. The maintenance projects are distributed across 12 districts in Hong Kong, Kowloon and the New Territories; some contracts have not yet been awarded, while others commenced or were completed before the investigation began.

The Competition Commission noted that this operation is a continuation of the first round of enforcement action in January this year. In that initial operation, 14 contractors and consultancy firms were searched, involving 17 maintenance projects with contracts totalling around HK$700 million. The Commission stated that, among the evidence obtained in that operation, a suspicious voicemail conversation was found indicating that another hidden bid-rigging group may exist, allegedly targeting a certain estate's maintenance project. According to the contents of the conversation, a contractor not originally within the scope of the investigation was suspected of contacting other contractors through an intermediary, requesting them to submit "cover" tenders during the bidding period for that estate's project, but was told that some contractors had already been approached by others to participate in bid-rigging for the same project.

After analysis, the Competition Commission found that the contractor was suspected of engaging in anti-competitive conduct in multiple projects, including distributing so-called "homework" — that is, instructions on bidding prices — to other contractors to manipulate tender outcomes. The conduct is alleged to constitute bid-rigging, market sharing, price-fixing conspiracies, and the exchange of sensitive information, in violation of the Competition Ordinance. The authority therefore took enforcement action against the contractor, other contractors involved and related parties; in addition to searching premises, it required all parties to produce documents and information, and to attend hearings to provide relevant materials. It is not appropriate at this stage to publicly disclose the subjects under investigation or the details of the case.
